newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma government sentences Suu Kyi relations.
newsitem.headline: Burma government sentences Suu Kyi relations.

text.p: Three Burmese democracy supporters, all of whom are related to opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi, were each sentenced to 10 years in prison, the Burmese government said in a statement on Sunday.

Suu Kyi's cousin and close aide Cho Aung Than, his sister Nge Ma Ma Than and her husband Myint Swe had been found guilty and sentenced under national security laws in Insein court in Rangoon, the statement said.
Several other close aides and family members of Suu Kyi's have been arrested and sentenced to long jail terms over the past 18 months as part of a crackdown against her movement.

"Cho Aung Than, Myint Swe and Nge Ma Ma Than have been sentenced for three years imprisonment for breaching the Unlawfaul Associations Act and a further seven years under the Emergency Provisions Act," the statement said.
The statement gave no further details. The three were detained in June and questioned in relation to smuggling videotapes of Suu Kyi's speeches abroad.
They have also been accused of being conduits for foreign funds the government said were received by Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy opposition party earlier this year, officials said.
In June Burma's military government, the State Law and Order restoration Council (SLORC), said Suu Kyi's party had received $82,200 from two Americans working for United States agencies.

In an interview last month Nobel Peace Laureate Suu Kyi strongly denied receiving the money. NLD Vice Chairman U Kyi Muang said in June the party had occasionally been offered money by foreign organisations but never accepts foreign donations as a matter of principle.
The Insein court also sentenced former sailor Myo Aung Thant to life imprisonment for high treason and terrorist-linked offences, the statement said.
Myo Aung Thant was convicted of attempting to smuggle explosives into Burma from Thailand earlier this year after being recruited by exiled Burmese dissidents, officials have said.
The SLORC has accused exiled pro-democracy groups of masterminding bomb attacks in Rangoon over the last few months, one of which killed the eldest daughter of a SLORC Army Chief of Staff Tin Oo.

The NLD won a landslide election victory in 1990 but the SLORC refused to recognise the result. Since Suu Kyi was released from six years house arrest in July 1995 the SLORC has detained and released several thousand NLD politicans and supporters.
